title: Symmetry introduction
examples: How do I check if something is symmetrical?
Can you show me a mirror line?

explain.say: Today we are learning about symmetry. Symmetry means something matches on both sides. Look at your hands. They look like mirror images, do they not?
We can check for symmetry using a folding test. Take this piece of paper and fold it carefully in half. Now, open it up and see the crease line.
This crease line is called the line of symmetry. If you fold it and the edges match perfectly, then the shape has symmetry. Try folding this butterfly shape now.
Another way to see symmetry is with a mirror. If you place a mirror here, the reflection must look exactly the same. This imaginary line is the mirror line.

faq.q: What is a line of symmetry?
faq.a: A line of symmetry is an imaginary line that divides a shape into two equal halves. If you fold the shape along this line, both sides will match up perfectly.
asks: Where is the line of symmetry?

faq.q: How do I use the folding test?
faq.a: To use the folding test, you gently fold the shape along the line you think is the symmetry. If the edges line up exactly, then it has symmetry.
asks: Can I fold it to check?
What does the folding test show?

faq.a: Yes, a heart shape usually has one line of symmetry going straight down the middle. The left side mirrors the right side.
No, not every shape has symmetry. A shape must be perfectly balanced on both sides to have a line of symmetry.
asks: What if it is not symmetrical?

faq.q: What is the difference between a mirror line and a line of symmetry?
faq.a: They are the same thing in math. Both are lines that divide a shape into two identical, matching halves. The mirror just helps us picture it.
asks: What is the other name for this line?

facts: Symmetry means that one side matches the other side.
The folding test helps us find the line of symmetry.
A line of symmetry can be straight or curved.
A butterfly shape has two lines of symmetry.

quiz.say: Which shape has a line of symmetry through the middle?
quiz.why: A circle is perfectly round, so any line drawn through its center works as a line of symmetry.

wrong.0: A triangle only has one line of symmetry if it is an isosceles triangle, not always.
wrong.1: A rectangle has two lines of symmetry, but the circle always has more.
wrong.3: A square has four lines of symmetry, but the circle is the only one listed that has infinite lines of symmetry.

quiz.say: If you fold this letter 'A' down the middle, what do you find?
quiz.why: The letter 'A' is symmetrical because the left side is a mirror image of the right side.

wrong.0: Folding does not cause the paper to tear if the shape is symmetrical.
wrong.1: Folding creates a crease, not just a bend, which shows the line of symmetry.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the letter 'A' is designed to be balanced on both sides.

quiz.say: A shape has symmetry when you can draw a line that...
quiz.why: The line of symmetry must divide the shape into two parts that are exactly the same.

wrong.0: The line can go diagonally or vertically, not just across.
wrong.1: Its length does not matter; only the balance of the halves matters.
wrong.2: It can be an imaginary line, so a ruler is not always needed.
